messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: inference-prod pool experiencing node flaps (NotReady) across us-west-2. >20% of nodes NotReady, multiple kubelet restarts detected. Escalation level: P1. Please ack and join #eng-oncall voice.
mia: acked. I'm oncall. joining voice. grabbing dashboard now.
ian: on it — looking at node events and recent deploys. no deploys in last 30m per deploy-bot.
jade: seeing lots of `kernel: oom_kill` and `kubelet[pid]: E070` in node logs. might be runaway process or driver instability. linking logs.
ian: paste: ```
$ kubectl get nodes -o wide | egrep "NotReady|Ready"
ip-10-0-12-7.us-west-2  NotReady  10d  v1.26.3  kubelet: Restarted 3x
ip-10-0-13-4.us-west-2  NotReady  8d   v1.26.3  kubelet: Restarted 2x
ip-10-0-14-2.us-west-2  Ready     12d  v1.26.3  
``` 
ian: and `kubectl describe node ip-10-0-12-7` shows repeated `kubelet: CRI runtime error` followed by `Back-off restarting kubelet`.
mia: early customer impact: 30% of inference pods in inference-prod pool are crashlooping or failed to schedule — backend metrics show increased 5xx and queueing latency. Not yet customer-wide, but a handful of tenants hitting timeouts.
carlos: adding context: this pool runs our 2x-A100 inference nodes for prod-lowlatency. If nodes go NotReady, autoscaler is slow because we hit instance launch quotas in the region.
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1775123456. Severity: P1. Pager duty: oncall-mia. Channel: #eng-oncall. Runbook: infra/kube-node-flap.
jade: short mitigation plan: 1) cordon the flapping nodes 2) drain safe pods with `--ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` 3) restart kubelet/systemd on affected hosts 4) shift traffic away from the pool via routing policy to dedicated standby pool. Doing step 1 now.
ian: commands:
```bash
kubectl cordon ip-10-0-12-7
kubectl drain ip-10-0-12-7 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
ssh ec2-user@ip-10-0-12-7 'sudo systemctl restart kubelet && sudo journalctl -u kubelet -n 200 --no-pager'
``` 
mia: doing the routing change with infra: `redwood-router set-weight inference-prod=0.5 => inference-dedicated=0.5` to start shifting load. will ramp slowly.
carlos: i'm increasing node group desired capacity by +3 to give buffer while we remediated flapping nodes. watch for quotas.
jade: noticed GPU driver messages: `nvidia-mig: device lost` and `nvidia: GPU rebooting` on one host. suspect driver/kernel mismatch after recent kernel patch. filing with infra.
ian: quick hotfix: set eviction threshold to free up memory pressure on nodes short-term: `kubectl patch cm kubelet-config -n kube-system --patch '{"data":{"evictionHard":"memory.available<200Mi"}}'` — rolling this carefully.
mia: recorded customer impact in incident doc: latency spikes for customers A, C, D between 12:04–12:12 UTC, a few 504s, no data exfiltration. Notifying CS to draft comms.
ops-bot: @here rotation update: SRE rotation handover scheduled in 45m. Please include remediation steps and impact summary.
sre-rotations: preparing handoff notes. Current state: 3 flapping nodes cordoned, 2 drained successfully, 1 failed drain due to local PV. Restarted kubelet on ip-10-0-12-7, it came back but reported `containerd: oom` and evicted some pods. Scaling in progress +3 nodes.
jade: manual workaround for local PV issue: moved PV-backed pods to standby node via `kubectl patch pod` with nodeSelector temporarily, then recreated PVCs on new node. risk low but manual.
ian: monitoring: token-heavy routes show 40% request fallback to shorter responses. Eng-console shows per-token cost spike as we hit fallback model. Carlos, should we reduce model size for routing to reduce failures? 
carlos: confirm: enabling fallback to 7B variant for non-SLA tenants. Doing that now via rollout policy: `redwood rollout set inference-prod --model=7b --traffic=20%`.
mia: live timeline note: first alert 1775123456 (12:03:12 UTC), major mitigation steps executed 12:04–12:15 UTC, routing change at 12:08 UTC, additional nodes up by 12:18 UTC. Monitoring for stability.
jade: infra update: reported driver bug to cloud vendor, they've opened ticket CV-984321. They suggested kernel rollback on affected AMI as long-term fix.
ian: logs showing kubelet stabilized on two nodes; one still flapping due to continuous OOM events. I'm creating a temp taint to keep workloads off it: `kubectl taint nodes ip-10-0-12-7 node-critical-flap=true:NoSchedule`.
mia: handover to next oncall: @sre-rotations will take next shifts. Key actions for follow-up: 1) confirm cloud quota isn't limiting autoscale 2) verify AMI/kernel rollbacks for affected node group 3) run postmortem on driver/kernel upgrade window 4) evaluate adding GPU-driver healthchecks.
sre-rotations: taking over. I'll monitor for 2h and coordinate postmortem. Adding post-incident checklist items to INC-2026-1775123456 doc.
ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-1775123456 status changed to: Mitigated — partial. Next: Postmortem and RCA.
ian: quick note: please collect `/var/log/syslog`, `/var/log/messages`, `journalctl -u kubelet`, and `nvidia-smi -q` from the three nodes we saw flapping. I'll stash them in S3 under s3://redwood-debug/INC-2026-1775123456/
mia: thanks team. I'll coordinate customer comms with CS and keep the channel updated. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: Reaction summary: :thumbsup: x3, :eyes: x2, :rotating_light: x1
